  • Government

A directory of the national ministries, departments and major agencies of the 27 EU member states plus the UK, Norway, Switzerland and Iceland, with their functions and official web links, modelled on the GOV.UK organisations directory. It includes an appendix of EU institutions and agencies, and SharePoint-ready versions (spreadsheet, CSV and page document).

  • 489 agencies
  • 28 EU bodies

European Government Departments and Agencies

National ministries, departments and major agencies of the 27 EU member states, the United Kingdom, Norway, Switzerland and Iceland — with their functions and official web links

Compiled 26 October 2026

Introduction

This directory covers 31 European countries: the 27 member states of the European Union plus the United Kingdom, Norway, Switzerland and Iceland. For each country it gives the official central-government portal, every current national ministry/department (530 in total), and a selection of 8–15+ major national agencies and regulators (489 in total) such as tax, statistics, police, medicines, data protection, telecoms, competition, environment and space bodies. An appendix lists the main EU institutions and agencies.

The structure is modelled on the UK government’s organisations directory (GOV.UK). For the UK, all ministerial and non-ministerial departments listed on GOV.UK are included, together with key executive agencies and public bodies.

Ministry lists reflect the cabinets in office as of 26 October 2026, checked against official government websites. Cabinets and ministry portfolios change frequently, after elections, coalition changes or reshuffles; where a country has a caretaker government or a very recent reorganisation this is noted at the top of its section. In federal or decentralised states (e.g., Germany, Austria, Belgium, Switzerland, Spain, Italy) only federal/national bodies are listed.

All links point to official government domains. Each link was checked with an automated HTTP request in October 2026. Many government sites block automated checks or are geo-restricted, so links are marked as follows:

  • † — the site answered but blocked or rejected the automated check (e.g., HTTP 403/503 bot protection); the domain is the official one and normally works in a browser.
  • ‡ — the site did not respond to the automated check (timeout, probably geo-blocking of the checking network); the domain is the official one.
  • Unmarked links returned a successful response.

Reference model: GOV.UK – Departments, agencies and public bodies

Belgium

Official government portal: belgium.be – Federal Public Services

Government (October 2026): Federal government of Bart De Wever (“Arizona” coalition) since February 2025. Belgian federal administration is organised into Federal Public Services (FPS/SPF/FOD) rather than ministries; ministers’ portfolios cut across FPSs. United Kingdom

Official government portal: GOV.UK – Departments, agencies and public bodies

Government (October 2026): Labour government of Prime Minister Keir Starmer. GOV.UK lists 23 ministerial departments, 20+ non-ministerial departments and 400+ agencies and public bodies; departmental names reflect machinery-of-government changes in 2025–26 (e.g., Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade; Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport). The agencies below are a curated selection of major executive agencies and public bodies.
